Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once sitting with Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) behind him when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) sought permission to enter and then entered (after permission was granted). Thereafter, Hadhrat Umar (RA) sought permission to enter and he also entered. Next came Hadhrat Sa'd bin Maalik (RA) who entered after seeking permission to do so. Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy talking to the others with his knees exposed when Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) sought permission to enter. Rasulullaah ﷺ then immediately covered his knees and told Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) to move away. After speaking for some time, the men left. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) then asked, "O Nabi of Allaah ﷺ! When my father and his companions entered, you did not place your clothes over your knees neither did you ask me to move away from you (why did you do so when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) came in?)."
Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Why should I not be shy in front of that person in front of whom even the angels are shy? I swear by the Being Who controls my life that the angels are shy for Uthmaan bin Affaan just as you are shy before Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ. Had he entered when you were close to me, he would neither speak nor raise his head until he left."[^2]
A Narration of Hadhrat Hasan Concerning the Modesty of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)

Speaking about the extreme modesty of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Hasan says, "Even though he was in a room behind a locked door, he would not remove his clothing to pour water over himself (when taking a bath). His modesty would prevent him from standing straight up (when bathing. He would therefore do so while sitting)."[^3]
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Be modest in front of Allaah. I cover my head out of modesty before Allaah even when I enter the toilet."[^4]
